Edema, Fluid Retention

Ailment edema fluid-retention circulatory lymphedema kidney heart

Evidence: peer_reviewed

Summary

Excess fluid accumulation in tissues causing swelling, typically in legs, ankles, or abdomen. Can be caused by heart conditions, kidney dysfunction, liver disease, or medication side effects.

Symptoms

  • swelling of extremities
  • pitting edema
  • weight fluctuation
  • shiny skin
  • reduced urine output

Other Treatment Options

  • Kidney Issues
    Kidney dysfunction affecting fluid balance and waste filtration, leading to fluid retention, edema, and metabolic imbalances.
  • Lymphedema
    Lymphatic system dysfunction causing chronic swelling, usually in arms or legs, when lymph fluid cannot drain adequately.
  • Gallbladder Issues / Gallstones
    Gallbladder dysfunction or gallstone formation causing digestion problems, bloating, and referred pain. Often linked to liver congestion.
  • Hypertension
    Chronic elevation of blood pressure in the arteries, increasing risk of heart disease, stroke, and kidney failure.
  • Heart Failure
    Cardiovascular condition where the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs, often causing fluid buildup and edema.
  • Chronic Kidney Disease
    Progressive kidney dysfunction that can lead to kidney failure, requiring dialysis or transplantation. Often causes severe edema and electrolyte imbalances.
  • UTI (Urinary Tract Infection)
    Infection in any part of the urinary system, commonly affecting the bladder and urethra. Characterized by burning pain, urgency, and frequent urination.
  • Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
    Chronic condition characterized by persistently elevated blood pressure in the arteries, increasing risk of cardiovascular events and kidney damage.
  • Kidney Stones
    Hard deposits of minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys and can cause severe pain when passing through the urinary tract.
  • Cardiovascular Disease
    Group of diseases affecting the heart and blood vessels, including coronary artery disease, heart failure, and stroke.
  • Liver Cirrhosis
    Chronic liver disease characterized by scarring (fibrosis) of liver tissue, affecting liver function and detoxification.
  • Lymphatic Congestion
    Poor lymphatic drainage leading to swelling, particularly in extremities.
  • Adrenal Fatigue
    Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysfunction leading to chronic fatigue and stress intolerance.
  • Immune System Weakness
    Weakened immune system leading to frequent infections and slow recovery.
  • Varicose Veins
    Enlarged, twisted veins typically in the legs due to poor venous circulation.
  • Anxiety & Stress

Treatment Approaches

  • Historical Traditional diuretic herbs (dandelion, celery seed, parsley) used for centuries to reduce swelling and support kidney function.
  • Proven Loop diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and aldosterone antagonists are evidence-based conventional treatments for edema secondary to heart, liver, or kidney disease.
  • Experimental CDS Protocol A (chlorine dioxide) explored anecdotally; no clinical evidence supports its use for edema reduction.
  • Conventional Compression stockings, low-sodium diet, and medical management of underlying cardiac, renal, or hepatic conditions.
